sentences.text: Shri Prashant Chourasia - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Aman Patel - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/ Stat Heard on admission.
Record of the Court below is received.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A. No. 16454 of 2023, which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

T h e appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC read with Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant and prosecutrix are well known to each other prior to the incident and trial Court committed error in calculating the age of the prosecutrix on the basis of scholar register.
There is no mention in the scholar register about date of birth of prosecutrix and there is no date of birth certificate of prosecutrix.
Age has been assessed on the basis of scholar register.
He further submitted that prosecutrix is above the age of fifteen years.
DNA report is negative.
Final hearing of this appeal would take sufficient long time.
Hence, prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.
I have heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and after hearing arguments of learned counsel for both the parties and perusal of the record, it is found that trial Court assessed the age of the prosecutrix on the basis of scholar register Lokesh Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76863095/
1 and date of birth certificate was not attached with the scholar register and P.W. 3 Upper Division Teacher who was examined in cross-examination mentioned the date of birth of scholar register on the basis of T.C.

sentences.text: So considering the fact that prosecutrix and appellant are known to each other prior to the incident and statement of P.W. 3, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the jail sentence of appellant deserves to be suspended.

Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A. No. 16454/2023, is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, i f not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court, the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended till final disposal of this appeal.
The appellant after being enlarged on bail shall mark his presence before the concerned trial Court on 22.02.2024 and thereafter on all subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
List the appeal for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
